name: HyperDex
tagline: Cornell's searchable distributed key-value store built on hyperspace hashing; dormant since 2016.
description: HyperDex was a distributed key-value and document store from Robert Escriva, Bernard Wong and Emin Gün Sirer at Cornell, presented at SIGCOMM 2012. Its central idea, hyperspace hashing, maps each object to a point in a multi-dimensional space defined by its attributes, so searches on secondary attributes contact only the servers covering that region instead of every node. Replicas are kept consistent with value-dependent chaining, giving linearizable operations and configurable fault tolerance, and a commercial extension, HyperDex Warp, added multi-key ACID transactions. Bindings covered C, C++, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, Node.js and Rust. Development stopped in 2016, and the hyperdex.org domain has since lapsed to an unrelated site.
statusNote: No commits since late 2016; hyperdex.org now hosts unrelated content. The authors' later work moved to Consus.
developer: Cornell University (Robert Escriva, Emin Gün Sirer)

pricing.notes: HyperDex Warp transactions were a separate commercial extension.

scale.notes: Objects are partitioned across a hyperspace of attribute subspaces with configurable replication.

strengths: Searches on secondary attributes touch only the relevant servers
Rich datatypes and atomic operations on documents
Peer-reviewed design with a permissive license
weaknesses: Abandoned since 2016; packages target old Linux distributions
Multi-key ACID transactions required the commercial Warp add-on
Original website and documentation domain lost
useCases: Studying multi-dimensional hashing for secondary search
notIdealFor: Projects needing support or security updates
